SETTING

PATIENT

| TASK

General Practice

You are an 18-year-old basketball player. You had a sudden severe pain at the
front of your left knee during practice. An ice pack was applied and you were
driven to the surgery by the team coach. Your knee is swelling and becoming very
painful especially if you try to walk or put your weight on it. You have been
experiencing pain in your knee for the last few days especially when you run or play
sport. You don’t remember injuring yourself, though your knee has been making a
clicking/popping sound and sometimes locks. You want to play on the weekend.

° Explain your current symptoms. Explain that you think the problem is just
‘growing pains’.

* Ask the doctor to fix your knee so that you will be able to play in the
competition.

® Ask for a spray to numb the pain and for painkillers.

* Try to convince the doctor that you will recover quickly because you are young
and fit.

* Be insistent as you want to play on the weekend, but eventually agree to follow
the doctor's advice.

CANDIDATE CARD NO. 2 MEDICINE

SETTING

DOCTOR

General Practice

You have just examined the patient, an 18-year-old basketball player who has been
brought to your surgery today by the team coach because of severe left knee pain.
You diagnose a meniscus tear (torn cartilage).

* Take a brief history from the patient.

¢ Explain the likely diagnosis of a meniscus tear in a way that he/she will
understand.

* Discuss immediate treatment (e.g., RICER regime — Rest, Ice, Compress,
Elevation and Referral to physiotherapist).

¢ Explain why pain medication is not effective on its own.

¢ Explain why you are referring the patient to a physiotherapist (e.g., appropriate
exercise plan, recovery strategy, specific treatments, etc.).

* Advise why he/she must not play sport until the pain has resolved and explain
what the consequences of ignoring this advice could be.

SETTING Suburban Clinic

PATIENT You are a 49-year-old accountant, married with two teenage children. You
presented three weeks ago with a one-month history of rectal bleeding, mild
diarrhoea and 2kg weight loss. The doctor requested a colonoscopy and today
you are returning for the results, Unfortunately, the doctor tells you that you have a
tumour in the bowel wall and the biopsy confirms cancer. The doctor recommends
urgent referral to a surgeon.

TASK * Become stunned by the news. You cannot believe that you have cancer. How
will you manage this? |

¢ Tell the doctor that your aunt died five years ago of bowel cancer and you saw
her suffer during chemotherapy. Make it clear you don’t want
chemo/radiotherapy.

e Express your concern about surgery: “Will | need a colostomy (stoma and bag)?”

¢ Seek reassurance that surgery will be beneficial: “Will surgery cure the cancer?”

“ OET NOVEMBER 2014
CANDIDATE CARD NO. 3 “MEDICINE

SETTING Suburban Clinic

DOCTOR Your patient is a 49-year-old accountant, married with two children. He/she
presented three weeks ago with a one-month history of rectal bleeding, diarrhoea
and 2kg weight loss. You requested a colonoscopy and today the patient is
retuming for the results. Unfortunately, the patient has a tumour in the descending
colon and the biopsy result confirms cancer,

TASK © Tell the patient the biopsy results (2cm tumour, confined to bowel wall) and
recommend urgent referral to a surgeon.

« Explain that management of the illness after surgery may include
chemo/radiotherapy, depending on the spread of the tumour (put only with |
patient’s consent). |

¢ Explain that a colostomy is unlikely as the tumour is confined to descending
colon.

* Encourage the patient to be optimistic about surgery (e.g., success rates are
usually high; biopsy indicates that tumour is limited to bowel wall).

SETTING Private Practice
PATIENT You are a 55-year-old aged care assistant. You injured your right elbow when you

were helping an overweight man out of his chair and he fell heavily onto you. Your
doctor is explaining your X-ray results to you.

* Ask the doctor to explain the X-ray results,

| © Cambridge Boxhill Language Assessment

Find out how long the injury will take to heal. Explain that you have a family to
support and you want to retum to your regular duties as soon as possible,
Become upset at the idea of taking time off work. You don't think that you can
afford to do this.

Be persuaded to return gradually to full duties via alternative duties (e.9., office
work, mentoring new staff, etc.).

Accept the doctor’s recommendation to take time off work and a prescription for
analgesics. Agree to visit again in two weeks.

You are an 88-year-old who iives independently. You have just received the results”

of tests performed on a urine sample which shows that you have a urinary tract
infection (UTI). You have had several UTIs recently, You are worried about the
recurrence and are discussing this ‘with your doctor.

Explain that you are sick of UTIs and want to take more precautions.

Tell the doctor that you eat well, with plenty of fresh fruit and vegetables. You
drink about two glasses of water and two coffees a day. You are otherwise fit,
healthy and very active; you walk for 15-30 minutes each day,

Find out what treatment the doctor suggests.

Seek reassurance that the suggested treatment will stop the infections recurring.

81

CANDIDATE CARD NO. 6 MEDICINE

SETTING

DOCTOR

TASK

Clinic

You are consulting an 88-year-old who lives Independently. You have just given the
results from a urine sample. The patient has a urinary tract infection (UTI) and has
had several proven UTIs recently. The patient ls concerned about the recurrence

and you are discussing some precautions. His/her general health is good
otherwise.

* Find out about the patient's diet, fluids, and exercise.

* Congratulate the patient on his/her healthy lifestyle, Highlight that good hygiene
is also important and educate the patient on ‘double voiding’ (e.g., emptying
bladder, waiting a moment then trying to empty again, etc.).

* Suggest treatment with antibiotics (e.g., prescription for trimethoprim 300
mg/day for three days, three month course of low dose nitrofurantoin, etc.).

* Reassure the patient that with dedication and patience you expect to be able to
resolve the current UTI issues.
